In the meantime, a few general measures that may help: take brief walking breaks every 30-45 minutes to avoid prolonged sitting, make sure your workstation has ergonomic support (feet flat on the floor, screen at eye level, lower back supported), try gentle stretching and low-impact activity like walking, and use heat or ice for 15-20 minutes depending on what feels better. Over-the-counter anti-inflammatories may provide temporary relief if you can safely take them. Seek prompt medical attention if you develop leg weakness, numbness in the groin or inner thighs, loss of bowel or bladder control, fever, unexplained weight loss, or if the pain follows a significant injury - these are red flags that warrant immediate evaluation. A clinician can help identify the specific cause and may recommend physical therapy or other targeted treatments.
